subject: geography
title: Carbon Cycle & Feedbacks
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on carbon cycle, slow and fast cycles, feedbacks.
final_note: Carbon links biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere.

concepts.def: Biological exchange across years-decades; photosynthesis, respiration.
Geological exchange over millions of years; weathering, volcanism.
Marine organisms sequester carbon into deep ocean via sinking detritus.
Capturing and storing carbon in biomass, soil, ocean or rocks.
Threshold beyond which sudden, irreversible change occurs.
Mechanism amplifying (positive) or dampening (negative) initial change.

walkthroughs.body_html: Photosynthesis fixes ~120 Gt/yr; respiration releases ~120 Gt/yr. Ocean exchanges ~90 Gt/yr each direction. Fast cycle responds within years to disturbance. Anthropogenic ~10 Gt/yr is small flux but accumulates because uptake doesn't fully balance emissions.

Volcanism returns 0.1 Gt/yr from mantle. Weathering removes CO2 via chemical reactions: CO2 + CaSiO3 -> CaCO3 + SiO2. Carbonate burial in marine sediments slowly stores carbon over millions of years. Long-term thermostat keeps Earth habitable.

Positive: ice-albedo loss accelerates warming; permafrost thaw releases 1500 Gt carbon stock. Negative: CO2 fertilisation may enhance plant uptake. Net effect uncertain but IPCC AR6 estimates feedbacks make warming 1.6-1.9x stronger than without them.

mcqs.q: Volcanism returns approximately how much carbon/yr?
